question: According to family systems theory, what happens when one family member falls seriously ill?

options.A: Daily household routines remain entirely unchanged
options.B: Family income automatically increases to cover treatment
options.C: The balance of the entire household is disrupted
options.D: The other members become completely immune to the disease

explanation: Because family members are closely linked, an illness in one person creates a ripple effect that impacts everyone in the home. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: How should a patient's palms face when they are in the standard anatomical position?

options.A: Facing forward
options.B: Facing backward
options.C: Facing each other
options.D: Facing upward

explanation: In the standard anatomical position, the arms rest at the sides with the palms turned forward and thumbs pointing outward. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T2#GNS111_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the very first link in the adult chain of survival?

options.A: Early recognition and call for help
options.B: Immediate high-quality chest compressions
options.C: Rapid use of an automated external defibrillator
options.D: Advanced life support by paramedics

explanation: Recognizing an emergency and activating the emergency response system quickly starts the entire rescue process. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which drug route is usually used when you cannot find an emergency IV line?

options.A: Intraosseous (IO)
options.B: Oral tablet swallowed
options.C: Topical skin patch
options.D: Subcutaneous injection

explanation: When an IV is impossible, we can drill right into the bone marrow (IO) to deliver emergency drugs super fast into circulation.

question: Why should a rehabilitation nurse avoid doing every single daily task for a patient?

options.A: It increases the risk of hospital-acquired infections
options.B: It stops the patient from regaining their independence
options.C: It violates standard medication administration policy
options.D: It causes immediate physical exhaustion for the nursing staff

explanation: Great nursing care means encouraging independence! If we do everything for our patients, they miss out on the practice they need to rebuild their strength.

question: What does it mean when the cervical dilation curve crosses the action line on a partograph?

options.A: The baby is ready to be delivered immediately
options.B: Labor is progressing faster than normal limits
options.C: Intervention or timely referral is urgently required
options.D: The mother has entered the fourth stage of labor

explanation: Crossing the action line signals prolonged labor, prompting healthcare workers to take corrective action or transfer the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h5)

question: What is a major cause of faecal incontinence among women in many resource-limited settings?

options.A: Obstetric trauma during childbirth
options.B: Weakness of the upper arm muscles
options.C: Excessive daily consumption of citrus fruits
options.D: Chronic overuse of inhaled medications

explanation: Difficult deliveries with untreated or poorly repaired perineal tears are a leading cause of sphincter damage and subsequent incontinence in women. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why do nurses try to avoid using a urinary catheter unless it's truly necessary?

options.A: It brings a high risk of introducing bacteria into the urinary tract
options.B: It is extremely painful for every patient who receives one
options.C: It requires surgical removal by a urologist
options.D: It permanently weakens the bladder muscles within hours

explanation: You got it! Because catheters bypass the body's natural defenses, they easily let germs in, making infections a big risk. That's why we only use them when we really have to.

question: What is the general long-term outlook for a patient who has a benign heart tumour completely removed?

options.A: Poor, with a life expectancy of only a few weeks
options.B: Hopeless without a full heart transplant
options.C: Guarded, because benign tumours always spread to the liver
options.D: Excellent, with most patients returning to normal activities

explanation: Once a benign tumour is successfully taken out, the cure rate is super high and patients usually get right back to their normal lives. Wonderful news for patients!

question: How does a home care nurse primarily evaluate adequate hydration and feeding in a newborn?

options.A: Checking the flexibility of the baby's finger joints
options.B: Weighing the baby before and after every single nursing session
options.C: Counting the number of wet and soiled diapers per day
options.D: Measuring the exact length of the infant every morning

explanation: Tracking wet diapers is a reliable, non-invasive way to ensure the newborn is receiving enough milk and staying hydrated. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of an incident report in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To provide permanent legal evidence for the patient's court case
options.B: To document safety events and improve institutional systems
options.C: To formally punish the specific nurse who made the mistake
options.D: To calculate the daily patient feeding and laundry costs

explanation: Incident reports aren't for witch hunts! They are learning tools to help the hospital spot recurring issues and make the ward safer for everyone.

question: Which type of range of motion exercise requires the patient to move their own joints to build strength?

options.A: Continuous passive motion
options.B: Active range of motion
options.C: Passive range of motion
options.D: Static stretching motion

explanation: Spot on! *Active* range of motion means the patient uses their own muscles, which helps maintain both joint flexibility and muscle strength.

question: You are about to flush out a deep infected wound that might splash fluid. What PPE do you need to wear?

options.A: Sterile gloves and a gown without eye protection
options.B: Gloves, a gown, a mask, and eye protection
options.C: A mask and shoe covers only
options.D: Gloves and a surgical cap only

explanation: Brilliant! Wound splashing is unpredictable. Covering your hands, body, mouth, and eyes keeps you totally protected. Safety first!

question: What should the nurse do first before having a patient step onto a mechanical weighing scale?

options.A: Measure the height of the patient
options.B: Ask the patient to drink a glass of water
options.C: Clean the platform with strong bleach solution
options.D: Check that the scale is zeroed on a flat surface

explanation: Ensuring the scale rests on a hard, level surface and points to zero prevents false readings. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why is breaking a massive problem down into tiny, bite-sized steps so helpful for an anxious patient?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any further nursing interaction
options.B: It guarantees that all hospital bills will be paid instantly
options.C: It proves to the doctor that the patient is fully cured
options.D: It restores a sense of personal control and reduces panic

explanation: Well reasoned! Big problems can make anyone freeze up. Small steps make the climb feel possible again and calm the nerves.

question: Which of these is a true feature of a polysynaptic reflex arc?

options.A: Total absence of a sensory neuron component
options.B: Presence of one or more interneurons
options.C: Involvement of only a single chemical synapse
options.D: Speed that is always faster than monosynaptic reflexes

explanation: Poly means many! These reflexes use one or more interneurons to handle slightly more detailed tasks, creating a few more connections along the path.

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance in community health?

options.A: To punish communities that fail to maintain basic sanitation
options.B: To eliminate all vector insects using chemical sprays
options.C: To detect and monitor disease patterns and potential reservoirs early
options.D: To manufacture and distribute expensive pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Surveillance is like our radar system—it helps nurses spot disease trends and catch outbreaks before they blow up.

question: What position is the patient usually placed in during a sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: Left lateral (Sims') position
options.B: Flat on their back (supine)
options.C: Sitting upright in a high chair
options.D: Flat on their stomach (prone)

explanation: You got it! Lying on the left side (Sims' position) naturally aligns the lower bowel, making the scope easier and safer to insert.

question: What happens if a vaccine meant for a muscle (intramuscular) is accidentally given into the fatty layer under the skin?

options.A: Severe systemic toxicity and high fever
options.B: Poor absorption leading to a weaker immune response
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the local muscle
options.D: Immediate destruction of the vaccine by skin enzymes

explanation: Fatty tissue doesn't have as rich a blood supply as muscle, so the vaccine doesn't get absorbed properly to do its job. Technique matters!

question: When do you typically hook up a humidification bottle filled with sterile water to an oxygen setup?

options.A: Only when the patient is diagnosed with an active lung infection
options.B: Whenever oxygen is delivered at any flow rate below one liter
options.C: When delivering higher flow rates that can dry the nasal passages
options.D: To cool the temperature of the gas before it enters the nose

explanation: Medical oxygen is very dry and can irritate the nose at higher flows. Adding sterile water for humidification keeps your patient nice and comfortable!

question: Which of these is an example of a research design rather than a tool?

options.A: A laboratory test tube used to check blood sugar
options.B: The overall structural framework of the study
options.C: A structured questionnaire handed to patients
options.D: An audio recording device used during an interview

explanation: Great job! The overall framework is your design, while items like questionnaires and test tubes are the physical tools you use inside that design.

question: What is the main job of capillaries in our blood circulation?

options.A: Exchanging gases and nutrients with body tissues
options.B: Storing extra blood volume during rest
options.C: Carrying blood away from the heart under high pressure
options.D: Preventing blood from flowing backward in the legs

explanation: Capillaries are super tiny vessels with very thin walls. This allows oxygen, food nutrients, and waste to pass easily between your blood and your body tissues!

question: Which of these is a well-known systemic autoimmune disease?

options.A: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
options.B: Grave's Disease
options.C: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
options.D: Hashimoto's Thyroiditis

explanation: Lupus (SLE) is classic for being systemic—it can affect the skin, joints, kidneys, and heart all at once!

question: What is the very first step you must perform before transferring a patient into a wheelchair?

options.A: Ask the patient to stand up without any assistance
options.B: Lock the wheels on the wheelchair and the bed
options.C: Place a heavy pillow directly on the wheelchair seat
options.D: Adjust the footrests to their highest setting

explanation: Locking the wheels prevents the furniture from sliding away when the patient puts their weight on it, stopping severe falls. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h4)

question: Why are peer educators so effective in adolescent health programs?

options.A: They are authorized to write prescriptions for antibiotics
options.B: Peer educators have medical degrees from universities
options.C: Young people often relate better to individuals in their own age group
options.D: Adults refuse to talk to anyone under twenty years old

explanation: Exactly! Teens share the same language and experiences, making peer educators trusted messengers who can easily connect with them.

question: In the SBAR communication tool, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

options.A: Bedside
options.B: Background
options.C: Behavior
options.D: Balance

explanation: Awesome! 'B' is for Background, which gives the history and context leading up to the current situation.

question: How did ancient Greek medicine under Hippocrates differ from earlier mystical approaches?

options.A: It prohibited the use of herbal remedies and plant extracts
options.B: It relied entirely on spiritual sacrifices and ritual prayers
options.C: It viewed disease as a natural process rather than divine punishment
options.D: It used modern laboratory testing and surgical antibiotics

explanation: Hippocrates and his followers shifted the focus toward rational observation of symptoms and natural causes of illness. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is it so important to check how a patient is feeling emotionally before teaching them about their medications?

options.A: Patients who are afraid will refuse to answer demographic survey questions
options.B: Fear and anxiety can prevent the patient from retaining instructions
options.C: Emotional distress changes the chemical makeup of oral medications
options.D: Anxious patients are more likely to experience drug allergies immediately

explanation: When someone is terrified or in pain, their brain is overloaded. Taking a moment to calm them down first helps them actually remember your teaching!

question: Why must community nurses look beyond the clinic when dealing with poor nutrition?

options.A: Because nutrition problems only exist inside large hospital wards
options.B: Because hospital management forbids nurses from talking about food
options.C: Because clinical medications can cure malnutrition completely on their own
options.D: Because root causes like poverty and food disruption require community-based action

explanation: Spot on! Nutritional challenges are often tied to bigger social and economic issues. Giving medicine alone isn't enough—we need community action and education too.

question: Two senior nurses are arguing bitterly over shift schedules, and the manager encourages both to give up a preferred off-day to meet in the middle. Which style is this?

options.A: Avoiding
options.B: Competing
options.C: Compromise
options.D: Collaboration

explanation: Compromise requires each person to concede something, resulting in a shared middle ground where neither gets everything they wanted. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of adolescent counseling corners in primary health centers?

options.A: Providing a safe space for youths to seek guidance on emotional struggles
options.B: Isolating sick children from the rest of the community
options.C: Providing mandatory legal representation for arrested teenagers
options.D: Holding young offenders in secure custody awaiting court trials

explanation: You got it! Counseling corners offer teenagers a confidential place to talk through stress and peer pressure before things get out of hand.

question: A child is prescribed 120 mg of a syrup. The stock bottle reads 120 mg per 5 mL. What volume should the nurse administer?

options.A: 10 mL
options.B: 12 mL
options.C: 2.5 mL
options.D: 5 mL

explanation: Using the formula: (120 mg / 120 mg) × 5 mL = 5 mL. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h5)

question: How do respiratory sympathomimetics actually cause bronchodilation?

options.A: They lower intracellular calcium to stop muscle contraction
options.B: They physically block mucus from entering the main bronchi
options.C: They increase the thickness of the airway lining walls
options.D: They stimulate the diaphragm to contract with more force

explanation: Calcium is what makes muscles squeeze tight. By lowering calcium levels inside the cells, these drugs stop the muscles from tightening up, keeping airways open!

question: When should a nurse refer a patient for genetic counseling regarding cancer?

options.A: The patient has a strong family history suggesting an inherited gene mutation.
options.B: The patient needs immediate chemotherapy for an active lung tumor.
options.C: The patient wants to quit smoking and needs nicotine replacement therapy.
options.D: The patient requires physical therapy to recover from radiation fatigue.

explanation: If a family history points to inherited genes, genetic counseling helps patients understand their risks and plan ahead.

question: Why do many follicles start growing at first, but usually only one reaches full maturity?

options.A: Only one ovary is allowed to work at a time
options.B: The body destroys all follicles except the very smallest one
options.C: One dominant follicle hogs the available supply of stimulating hormones
options.D: Infections wipe out the rest of the growing eggs

explanation: Think of it as a competition! The dominant follicle grabs the most hormonal support, causing the others to stop growing and fade away. You're doing great learning this!

question: Which surgical treatment uses plates and screws attached directly to the bone to fix a fracture?

options.A: Open reduction internal fixation
options.B: Closed manual manipulation
options.C: External pin stabilization
options.D: Skin traction therapy

explanation: We call this ORIF! The surgeon opens the site to see the bone clearly, then uses internal hardware like metal plates and screws to hold everything tightly in place.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard criterion for patient selection before granting leave?

options.A: Presence of a supportive family or safe living arrangement
options.B: Having a large financial inheritance waiting outside
options.C: Demonstrated stability of acute psychiatric symptoms
options.D: Reliable cooperation with medication regimens

explanation: Money doesn't determine clinical readiness! Stability, safe housing, and taking medications are what truly matter for a successful leave.

question: Why is food safety especially important for individuals living with HIV?

options.A: Unsafe food stops the body from absorbing any vitamins
options.B: Contaminated food directly neutralizes antiretroviral medications
options.C: It prevents the sudden development of severe food allergies
options.D: Their weakened immune systems are more vulnerable to infections

explanation: Correct! Because the immune system may be compromised, patients can catch foodborne and waterborne illnesses much more easily.

question: How does a vasectomy change a man's semen volume after surgery?

options.A: It becomes completely clear and watery
options.B: It stays almost exactly the same
options.C: It drops to zero immediately
options.D: It increases to make up for lost sperm

explanation: Spot on! Sperm only make up a tiny fraction of semen, so blocking their path doesn't noticeably change the amount of fluid.

question: A ward manager notices staff are burning out and making mistakes on night shifts due to bad scheduling. What should be done first?

options.A: Stop holding shift handovers to save working time
options.B: Punish the nurses for making clinical errors during the night
options.C: Increase the number of patients assigned to each nurse
options.D: Redesign the roster to balance shift distribution and staff skill mix

explanation: Brilliant choice! When scheduling causes fatigue and errors, the best fix is to address the root problem by making a fairer, safer roster.

question: How do deep, widespread fungal infections often show up in lung tissue scans?

options.A: As watery blisters covering the outer skin layer
options.B: As acute pus-filled abscesses with rapid cell rupture
options.C: As a gray pseudomembrane blocking the trachea
options.D: As granulomatous lesions that resemble tuberculosis

explanation: Fungi love to form granulomas in the lungs just like TB does, which can sometimes make them tricky to tell apart on an X-ray!

question: Why are faith-based health clinics so important in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: They possess unlimited budgets from foreign governments
options.B: They charge the highest fees for specialized surgeries
options.C: They frequently establish hospitals in remote and underserved areas
options.D: They focus exclusively on urban corporate executives

explanation: Faith-based groups have a long history of setting up clinics in rural or hard-to-reach places where government hospitals might not have reached yet.

question: Why might a nurse choose to use 'avoidance' during a heated ward argument?

options.A: To let intense emotions cool down before attempting discussion
options.B: To permanently ignore the underlying hospital policy
options.C: To prove that the other person was completely right
options.D: To win the argument without speaking a single word

explanation: Stepping away for a moment isn't always running away; sometimes it's the smartest way to let hot tempers cool off.

question: How does qualitative data analysis differ from quantitative analysis?

options.A: Qualitative analysis looks for recurring themes in text rather than numbers
options.B: Qualitative analysis ignores patient words and focuses on lab values
options.C: Qualitative analysis uses computer software to run complex regressions
options.D: Qualitative analysis requires strict mathematical proof of significance

explanation: Instead of crunching numbers, qualitative researchers read through text to find common patterns and themes in what people said.

question: A patient comes in complaining of a heavy, squeezing chest pressure spreading to their jaw while doing chores. What does this classic sign point to?

options.A: Gastric acid reflux
options.B: Pulmonary infection
options.C: Myocardial ischemia
options.D: Musculoskeletal strain

explanation: Brilliant! Exertional chest pressure that travels to the jaw is a classic textbook warning sign that the heart muscle isn't getting enough oxygen.

question: What vital sign must you watch most carefully after giving an IV opioid?

options.A: Oxygen saturation only
options.B: Respiratory rate
options.C: Capillary refill
options.D: Body temperature

explanation: Safety first! Opioids can slow down the brain's breathing center, making your respiratory check the most important assessment in the room.

question: A 14-year-old girl wants to stay in school, but her uncle insists she accept an arranged marriage. Which social dynamic is primarily at play here?

options.A: An educational shortage of secondary school teachers
options.B: Patriarchal control over female autonomy and decision-making
options.C: A temporary government policy supporting adolescent labor
options.D: A religious mandate requiring early entry into the workforce

explanation: Correct! When male relatives override a young girl's personal dreams and choices, it shows a classic patriarchal structure in action.

question: What is the safe temperature range for storing routine vaccines like Pentavalent and PCV in a clinic refrigerator?

options.B: +2°C to +8°C

explanation: Routine diluents and liquid vaccines like Pentavalent and PCV must be kept cool between two and eight degrees Celsius and never frozen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h5)

question: What exactly is an adverse event in healthcare?

options.A: A patient refusing to take prescribed medication
options.B: A natural progression of a terminal disease
options.C: A normal side effect expected from surgery
options.D: An unintended injury caused by medical care

explanation: You've got this! An adverse event is simply unexpected harm that happens because of medical treatment, not from the disease itself.

question: Which part of the respiratory tract filters out large particles before they reach the lungs?

options.A: The upper airway and nose
options.B: The pulmonary alveoli
options.C: The terminal bronchioles
options.D: The visceral pleura

explanation: The nasal passages and upper airway warm, humidify, and filter incoming air, catching larger debris and particles. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the main goal of a patient referral system in reproductive health?

options.A: Connecting community-level needs with clinical care without losing patients in transit
options.B: Punishing healthcare workers who fail to meet monthly consultation targets
options.C: Ensuring every patient is admitted to a tertiary teaching hospital immediately
options.D: Tracking the financial profits of private maternity hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Referral systems make sure that when a patient needs more advanced care, they are safely guided to the right place without falling through the cracks.

question: What is a major barrier to price transparency in many healthcare markets?

options.A: Patients are legally barred from asking about expenses
options.B: Hospitals update their price lists every minute
options.C: Final costs are often hidden or unknown until after treatment
options.D: All medical treatments cost the exact same amount globally

explanation: Opaque billing and complex negotiations make it very difficult for patients to know service costs upfront. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is cultural awareness so important for nursing students?

options.A: Nurses care for diverse patients from many different backgrounds
options.B: It stops students from ever arguing about medical facts
options.C: Lecturers grade you based on your cultural heritage
options.D: The hospital requires everyone to speak three local languages

explanation: As a nurse, you will meet patients from all walks of life. Understanding their cultures helps you give kind, respectful care to everyone.

question: What is the main problem when a mother loses her child's immunization card?

options.A: An automatic fine issued by the local health department
options.B: Immediate development of vaccine-preventable diseases in the infant
options.C: The child losing all previous immunity built by past doses
options.D: Difficulty knowing which future vaccines the child needs and when

explanation: Exactly! Without the card, it's hard to tell for sure which doses the baby has already received and when the next one is due.

question: A patient collapses in the hospital hallway. What is the maximum time a nurse should spend checking for normal breathing?

options.A: 30 seconds
options.B: 1 minute
options.C: 2 minutes
options.D: 10 seconds

explanation: Keep it quick! Spend no more than 10 seconds checking for breathing so you don't delay starting chest compressions.

question: Which supplement is very important during early pregnancy to prevent neural tube defects?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Potassium chloride
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Folic acid

explanation: Folic acid is a prenatal superstar! It protects the baby's developing brain and spine in the early weeks.

question: What is the most important screening test nurses should encourage to catch early cell changes on the cervix?

options.A: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.B: Pap smear
options.C: CA-125 blood test
options.D: Endometrial biopsy

explanation: The Pap smear is a simple, life-saving screening tool that lets us spot weird cellular changes on the cervix long before they ever turn into cancer.

question: What is the primary role of a community health nurse working in a rural Nigerian primary health center?

options.A: Providing preventive education, immunizations, and basic curative care
options.B: Operating an advanced trauma surgery unit for major accidents
options.C: Managing financial investments for private pharmaceutical companies
options.D: Enforcing strict medical laws from a desk in the federal capital

explanation: Nigerian nurses in primary care focus on grassroots prevention, maternal-child health, and treating common illnesses. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h8)

question: Why must you cross-check delivery notes with actual physical supplies before paying a vendor?

options.A: It guarantees that the supplier will offer a discount on the next order
options.B: It automatically updates the expiration dates of the received medications
options.C: It prevents paying for items that were billed but never actually delivered
options.D: It satisfies the legal requirement for filing annual income taxes

explanation: Always count what's in the box! Checking physical goods against the invoice protects the hospital from paying for items that were left out or short-supplied.

question: When is the correct time to document that you have given a medication?

options.A: Before walking into the patient's room to prepare the drugs
options.B: Immediately after giving the medication to the patient
options.C: At the very end of the working shift before going home
options.D: Whenever another colleague reminds you to update the chart

explanation: Chart right away after administration! Doing it immediately prevents accidental double-dosing and keeps the patient's records accurate.

question: Why might relying only on the hospital's liability insurance leave you unprotected as a nurse?

options.A: Institutional coverage automatically pays out cash settlements directly to the nurse
options.B: Hospital attorneys represent the institution and may have interests conflicting with the nurse's
options.C: Employer policies never cover mistakes made during night shifts
options.D: Facility insurance policies expire the moment a nurse takes a short break

explanation: Remember, the hospital's legal team works for the hospital, not you! Their main job is protecting the facility, so having your own backup is smart nursing practice.

question: What is the gold standard test to confirm a diagnosis of lymphoma?

options.A: Complete blood count
options.B: Excisional lymph node biopsy
options.C: Routine skin scraping
options.D: Fine-needle aspiration cytology

explanation: To be 100% sure, pathologists need to look at a whole lymph node under the microscope. Taking out the node (excisional biopsy) is the best way to do this.

question: An adult patient needs ear drops for an infection. How should you pull their outer ear (auricle) to straighten the ear canal?

options.A: Pull the earlobe straight down toward the chin
options.B: Push the tragus forward tightly
options.C: Pull the auricle upward and outward
options.D: Tilt the entire head sideways without touching the ear

explanation: For adults, gently pulling the ear up and back straightens the canal so the drops flow all the way down smoothly.

question: Which of these actions is a major safety violation when storing medical waste in a hospital?

options.A: Locking the storage room door at night
options.B: Placing biohazard warning signs outside
options.C: Using a well-ventilated utility room
options.D: Leaving bags in public hospital corridors

explanation: Exactly right! Medical waste should never sit in public hallways where patients, visitors, or staff could trip over, knock over, or tear the bags.

question: What does trauma-informed care involve when nursing an FGM survivor?

options.A: Explaining procedures clearly and asking permission before any physical examination
options.B: Focusing strictly on physical healing while ignoring emotional concerns
options.C: Insisting that family members stay in the room during all treatments
options.D: Avoiding physical exams entirely to prevent any uncomfortable memories

explanation: Trauma-informed care builds trust by giving patients control and minimizing distress during sensitive examinations. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is a strict, mandatory rule when offering HCT to a client?

options.A: Financial clearance before testing can begin
options.B: Automatic police notification for reactive cases
options.C: Mandatory public announcement of positive results
options.D: Voluntary informed consent from the client

explanation: Great job! A client must always willingly agree to take the test after understanding what it involves, with zero force or pressure.

question: What is a common dietary trap patients fall into when starting a low-fat diet?

options.A: Eating too many leafy green vegetables every day
options.B: Consuming too much lean skinless chicken breast
options.C: Replacing healthy fats with large amounts of sugary foods
options.D: Drinking excessive amounts of plain filtered water

explanation: When foods lose their fat content, they can taste bland. Patients often make the mistake of loading up on sweets and refined carbs to compensate, which messes with blood sugar.

question: What is a safe, effective substitute to enhance flavor without adding sodium?

options.A: Fresh garlic, ginger, and local herbs
options.B: Baking soda and chemical preservatives
options.C: Extra helpings of commercial seasoning cubes
options.D: Table salt mixed with white sugar

explanation: Aromatics like garlic and ginger provide strong flavors and aromas that compensate for a lack of salt. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge faced by national disaster agencies?

options.A: Poor road networks and heavy traffic congestion during crises
options.B: Excessive funding and overabundance of modern rescue equipment
options.C: Infrastructural violations like buildings blocking natural waterways
options.D: Inadequate financial support and poor resource allocation

explanation: Sadly, disaster agencies usually struggle with a shortage of funds and equipment, rather than having too much! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h7)

question: What is the correct order for examining a patient's bones, joints, and muscles?

options.A: Palpation, inspection, then range of motion
options.B: Range of motion, palpation, then inspection
options.C: Palpation, range of motion, then inspection
options.D: Inspection, palpation, then range of motion

explanation: Always look first (inspect), feel second (palpate), and test movement last. This stops you from causing extra pain before your exam is done!

question: A nurse researcher wants to prove that a new wound care protocol prevents infections better than the old method without relying on messy old records. Which study design should be chosen?

options.A: Prospective design
options.B: Cross-sectional snapshot
options.C: Case-control past analysis
options.D: Retrospective chart review

explanation: A prospective design allows the researcher to implement the protocol today and record infection rates moving forward with high accuracy. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h3)

question: How is child trafficking different from regular help on a family farm?

options.B: Trafficking only happens in urban city centers

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of family dysfunction or distress?

question: What causes Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)?

question: What exactly are intrinsic sugars?

options.A: Sugars naturally bound inside the cell walls of whole foods

options.C: Refined sweeteners added to foods during factory processing
options.D: Artificial sweeteners that contain zero calories

question: Why do constant interruptions while preparing medications make errors much more likely?

options.B: Interruptions force the nurse to work faster than normal speed
options.C: Interruptions disrupt short-term memory and cause dose calculation slips
options.D: Interruptions automatically invalidate the doctor's prescription

question: What part of the cardiovascular system do antiarrhythmic medications target?

options.B: The total volume of circulating blood plasma

question: Why do patients with celiac disease often have fatty, bulky stools (steatorrhea)?

question: Why must you always check two patient identifiers (like name and hospital number) before giving an injection?

options.B: To ensure the right medication goes to the right person

question: A community health nurse in a rural Nigerian clinic notices an increase in severe watery diarrhea cases. What is the most immediate nursing action?

question: Why is a longitudinal design great for studying chronic illnesses like heart disease?

options.A: It costs almost no money compared to other study methods

question: Why is it important to write clear behavioral details in your notes instead of vague words?

options.A: To guarantee that the patient is discharged without home care

options.C: To replace the need for verbal shift-to-shift report handoffs
options.D: To reduce the total number of nursing shifts required in a week

explanation: Writing exact details prevents guesswork and helps every nurse on the team track whether the patient is getting better or worse.

question: A nurse is getting the delivery room ready for an expected birth. What should be checked first?

options.A: Dimming all room lights to create a relaxing sleep environment
options.B: Staging extra visitor chairs around the bed for family members
options.C: Checking that emergency resuscitation equipment and oxytocin are ready

question: What is the main idea behind performance-based financing in health aid?

options.A: Government budgets are approved without any review of previous hospital spending
options.B: Donors pay hospitals based on the total number of physical buildings they own
options.C: Funds are released only after verifying specific health service outcomes

question: Which nail change is most commonly linked to long-term low blood oxygen levels?

question: What must a nurse obtain from a community member before conducting an individual health interview or examination?

question: Calcium, potassium, and iron belong to which group of nutrients?

question: Which type of drug reaction specifically needs the patient to have been exposed to the drug before?

options.A: Allergic reaction

options.D: Cumulative drug effect

question: Why do teenagers sometimes make impulsive choices or take big risks?

options.C: The body produces too much calcium during early puberty growth spurts

question: Which nursing action shows safe and professional use of the partograph?

question: Why does cigarette smoking put a woman at a higher risk of developing cervical cancer?

question: Why do nurses working in disaster zones need to understand how search and rescue operations work?

question: What is one of the biggest challenges to infection control in busy Nigerian healthcare settings?

question: What is meant by a disease 'reservoir'?

options.A: Where the infectious agent normally lives and multiplies

options.C: A device used to measure patient body temperature
options.D: The specific medication given to kill a virus

question: What is a major nursing concern when an older adult has severe dental problems and missing teeth?

options.A: Increased likelihood of developing hypertension

question: You just collected a wound swab from a patient with a leg ulcer. What's the best immediate step?

question: In healthcare, what does the term 'biological sex' refer to?

question: Why is promoting local Nigerian foods better than relying on foreign supplements for community health?

question: In global polio campaigns, what does the abbreviation 'AFP' stand for?

question: Why do we as nursing students need to look back at the history of nutrition?

question: What is the main job of the fimbriae (the finger-like ends of the fallopian tube)?

question: What does Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) measure?

question: Which of the following is a common health risk linked to traditional masculine norms?

question: Why do quality improvement projects usually start on a small scale instead of rolling out hospital-wide?

question: What is the main benefit of using Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT) when trying to quit?

question: Which group of vitamins needs dietary fat to be properly absorbed by the body?

question: A 15-year-old patient refuses to discuss their mental health with parents but opens up completely to a school track coach. How should the nurse respond?

question: Why is follow-up after a referral so important for a community health nurse?

question: Why is teaching patients preventive self-care so crucial before they leave the hospital?

question: Why is it important for public health teams to supply food and basic items to households in strict quarantine?

question: What is the main idea behind health insurance schemes like the NHIA?

question: What is one of the biggest duties of a community health nurse when dealing with NCDs?

question: What is the main difference between anonymity and confidentiality in research?

question: Why do junior nurses often ask a veteran nurse for advice even though she has no official management title?

question: Why is it important to avoid heavy clinical jargon when reporting disaster monitoring data to non-medical coordinators?

question: How do benzimidazole drugs mainly attack parasitic worms?

question: What is the primary public health goal of nurse-led immunization services in primary clinics?

question: What is the protective protein shell enclosing a virus's genetic material called?

question: Why do doctors avoid doing a direct needle biopsy of a heart mass?

question: What is a fixed cost in a health care facility?

question: Why is the link between poor nutrition and infections called a vicious cycle?

question: Which parts of the brain are hit hardest by GPI?

question: How do teenagers typically react when adults respond to adolescent mistakes with harsh anger and judgment?

question: What is the main idea behind the famous 'Swiss Cheese Model' in healthcare?

question: What is the main goal of contact tracing when an infectious disease breaks out?

question: What is the main purpose of a home visit in community nursing?

options.C: Blood flows rapidly through the cervix as bright red fluid
options.D: The placenta detaches silently without any pain or bleeding whatsoever

explanation: In a concealed abruption, blood gets trapped inside the uterus. This means external bleeding looks deceptively small while internal shock can develop quickly. Great job keeping this in mind!

question: Which muscle tissue type is under voluntary control?

options.A: Skeletal muscle
options.B: Visceral muscle
options.C: Cardiac muscle
options.D: Smooth muscle

explanation: Skeletal muscles attach to bones and allow conscious, voluntary control over body movements. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h1)

question: What critical assessment must a nurse make before administering ear drops?

options.A: Check the patient's blood pressure and pulse
options.B: Confirm that the eardrum is intact
options.C: Test the patient's hearing using a tuning fork
options.D: Measure the exact width of the ear canal

explanation: Putting drops into an ear with a ruptured eardrum can cause severe pain and push infection deeper into the inner ear. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which hormone tells the kidneys to hold onto water when the body is getting dehydrated?

options.A: Antidiuretic hormone
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: You got it! Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) tells your renal tubes to reabsorb water so you don't lose too much in your urine.

question: What is the ultimate aim of dietary counselling?

options.A: Immediate cure of chronic viral infections
options.B: Total elimination of carbohydrates from the diet
options.C: Behavioral change regarding food habits
options.D: Reducing hospital kitchen operational costs

explanation: The main goal is to help patients change their actual eating behaviors for better long-term health outcomes. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h2)

question: When is the risk of getting pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) highest after an IUD insertion?

options.A: Only if the client gets pregnant with the IUD
options.B: During the first 20 days after insertion
options.C: There is never any risk of infection
options.D: After the IUD has been in place for five years

explanation: Because tiny amounts of bacteria can accidentally enter the uterus during the procedure, the infection risk is highest right after insertion, during the first few weeks.

question: Which piece of patient history is most critical for a nurse to check before a skin snip?

options.A: A history of bleeding disorders or anticoagulant use
options.B: Previous surgery for appendicitis years ago
options.C: Mild seasonal allergies to pollen and dust
options.D: A childhood diagnosis of uncomplicated asthma

explanation: Safety first! Because a skin snip involves a tiny cut, we always check if the patient bleeds easily or takes blood thinners.

question: Why might a nurse experience ethical conflict when carrying out a patient's request to stop life support?

options.A: Fearing that the hospital will refuse to pay the nurse's salary
options.B: Believing that living wills have no legal standing in a hospital
options.C: Balancing the duty to do no harm with the duty to respect patient choices
options.D: Knowing that doctors are legally required to ignore advance directives

explanation: Nurses want to protect life, so stopping life support can feel emotionally difficult even though respecting the patient's autonomy is legally and ethically correct. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h4)

question: Which joint works just like a door hinge, letting you bend and straighten your elbow?

options.A: Condyloid joint
options.B: Saddle joint
options.C: Hinge joint
options.D: Pivot joint

explanation: Spot on! Hinge joints (like your elbow and knee) move back and forth smoothly in just one main direction.

question: A patient suddenly falls asleep during the day and feels weak when feeling strong emotions. What condition is this?

options.A: Insomnia
options.B: Narcolepsy
options.C: Somnambulism
options.D: Sleep apnea

explanation: Narcolepsy causes sudden sleep attacks during the day. Strong emotions can sometimes trigger sudden muscle weakness called cataplexy.

question: A stroke patient can walk with a walker, but struggles to button their shirt. Which team member should help with this?

options.A: The occupational therapist
options.B: The physical therapist
options.C: The speech-language pathologist
options.D: The vocational case manager

explanation: Occupational therapists (OTs) love working on everyday tasks! They specialize in fine motor skills like dressing, grooming, and feeding.

question: A nutrient crosses the intestinal lining with the help of a carrier protein, moving down its concentration gradient without using ATP. What is this called?

options.A: Pinocytosis
options.B: Facilitated diffusion
options.C: Simple diffusion
options.D: Active transport

explanation: You nailed it! Facilitated diffusion is like getting a helpful push down a slide—it uses proteins to make the trip easier, but doesn't require any cellular energy.

question: What is the ultimate goal of home health nursing?

options.A: Replacing all family involvement in patient care
options.B: Helping the patient achieve maximum independence
options.C: Transferring the patient to a permanent nursing home
options.D: Keeping the patient dependent on daily nursing visits

explanation: Home health nursing focuses heavily on empowering patients to manage their own care and daily routines safely. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T5#GNS324_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which type of laxative is generally safe in pregnancy because it draws water into the stool to soften it?

options.A: Strong chemical purgatives
options.B: Raw castor oil blends
options.C: Stool softeners and bulk-forming laxatives
options.D: High-dose mineral oil enemas

explanation: Spot on! Gentle agents like docusate or psyllium work naturally without irritating the womb, making them safe choices for expectant mums.

question: What is a huge risk factor for depression in older adults?

options.A: Having too many visiting family members
options.B: Social isolation and loneliness
options.C: Participating in regular group exercise classes
options.D: Living in a community with active social clubs

explanation: Being cut off from people takes a heavy toll on mental and physical health. Connection is medicine!

question: What part of a mature sperm cell contains the enzymes needed to penetrate an egg?

options.A: The acrosome
options.B: The midpiece
options.C: The nucleus
options.D: The flagellum

explanation: The acrosome sits atop the head of the sperm and releases digestive enzymes to break through the protective layers of the oocyte. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy on a thyroid lump?

options.A: To obtain cells for microscopic examination to check for cancer
options.B: To inject radioactive isotopes directly into the thyroid tissue
options.C: To completely remove the entire thyroid gland without surgery
options.D: To measure the 24-hour baseline hormone production levels

explanation: Spot on! An FNA takes a tiny sample of cells so the lab can check them under a microscope to confirm or rule out cancer.

question: Which finding in a patient should immediately trigger a referral rather than continued standing order treatment?

options.A: A small healed skin scratch on the arm
options.B: A mild low-grade fever with normal breathing
options.C: A request for routine health education
options.D: Signs of severe shock or unresponsiveness

explanation: Severe signs like shock or unresponsiveness exceed primary care capacity and require urgent escalation to a higher facility. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h8)

question: Which of these actions goes AGAINST a nurse's ethical duties?

options.A: Sharing patient medical details on social media
options.B: Advocating for the best interests of the sick person
options.C: Protecting patient privacy and medical confidentiality
options.D: Respecting the cultural beliefs of every patient

explanation: Correct! Patient confidentiality is sacred. Sharing patient details online is a serious breach of ethics and professional trust.

question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in the SMART criteria for objective formulation?

options.A: Moderate
options.B: Manageable
options.C: Mandatory
options.D: Measurable

explanation: In SMART planning, objectives must be measurable so the team can prove whether they achieved them or not. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h4)

question: Why do multiple body systems react when something like blood pressure drops too low?

options.A: Only the nervous system is capable of fixing blood pressure.
options.B: Organ systems depend on each other to maintain internal balance.
options.C: The body shuts down all systems to conserve remaining energy.
options.D: Organs act independently without communicating with one another.

explanation: Spot on! Because our body systems are closely linked, a drop in pressure triggers teamwork across nerves, heart, and kidneys to restore normal levels.

question: A patient falls and cracks the hard outer layer of their thigh bone (femur). Which bone tissue is affected?

options.A: Compact bone
options.B: Cartilaginous bone
options.C: Trabecular bone
options.D: Spongy bone

explanation: Compact bone forms that tough, dense outer shield of long bones. You'll see this often in orthopaedic wards!

question: A patient who lost their job six months ago visits the clinic complaining of constant headaches and stomach aches with no clear medical cause. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: A rare genetic blood disorder
options.B: An acute bacterial infection
options.C: A reaction to routine childhood immunizations
options.D: Somatic symptoms of underlying psychological stress

explanation: Spot on! People facing job loss often express emotional distress through physical aches, known as somatic symptoms. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h2)

question: What is the most important first step when assessing a newly met street child?

options.A: Building trust through a non-judgmental and patient approach
options.B: Documenting their home address for official taxation
options.C: Immediately calling law enforcement to detain the minor
options.D: Insisting on immediate blood draws for laboratory tests

explanation: Brilliant nursing logic! Because these kids are used to being mistreated, you have to win their trust before they will let you help them.

question: A patient feels a burning, shooting pain down their leg after a back injury. What kind of pain is this?

options.A: Visceral nociceptive pain
options.B: Neuropathic pain
options.C: Referred inflammatory pain
options.D: Acute somatic pain

explanation: Burning, tingling, or shooting pains are classic signs of neuropathic pain, which happens when nerves themselves are irritated or damaged.

question: As a nurse leader, why is it important to understand the psychology behind workplace changes?

options.A: To completely eliminate all feelings of stress in the hospital
options.B: To ensure that no clinical protocols are ever modified again
options.C: To view resistance as a normal reaction instead of laziness
options.D: To punish staff members who fail to adopt new policies

explanation: Spot on! When leaders understand this, they can approach staff hesitation with empathy and support rather than frustration.

question: During a home visit at 34 weeks, you notice the home has no clean running water or good lighting. What is your best move?

options.A: Ignore the issue since delivery is still weeks ahead
options.B: Help the family plan how to store clean water and arrange good lighting for the birth
options.C: Advise the mother to move to a relative's house in another town
options.D: Cancel the home birth plan immediately without discussing alternatives

explanation: As a supportive nurse, you help problem-solve practical needs with the family ahead of time so they are fully ready for the big day.

question: What is the main goal when a patient with chronic Hepatitis C is given direct-acting antiviral medications?

options.A: To temporarily relieve itching caused by high blood pressure
options.B: To replace the damaged liver tissue with artificial cells
options.C: To boost the patient's appetite and promote rapid weight gain
options.D: To cure the infection and prevent long-term liver scarring

explanation: Modern medicines are wonderful—these direct-acting antivirals aim to completely kick the Hepatitis C virus out of the body and stop further damage.

question: Which of these is a bad practice when looking at clinical data?

options.A: Looking at trends over several months instead of one week
options.B: Ignoring the denominator when looking at small sample sizes
options.C: Reviewing how patient data was collected in the first place
options.D: Checking whether two events are truly related before acting

explanation: Well done! Forgetting the total number of patients can make a tiny issue look like a massive epidemic. Always check the whole picture!

question: Which hormone is mostly responsible for preparing the lining of the womb for implantation?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Well done! Progesterone takes the lead in the second half of the cycle, making the womb lining thick and cozy for a potential pregnancy.

question: Why is it so important to involve community members during the planning stage of a health program?

options.A: It ensures the program respects local culture and actual needs
options.B: It guarantees that funding will come from international donors
options.C: It removes the need for any evaluation at the end
options.D: It allows the nurse to avoid attending community meetings

explanation: When people help plan their own health programs, they take ownership and the project is much more likely to succeed.

question: Which type of germ is the absolute hardest to kill with standard chemical disinfectants?

options.A: Vegetative bacteria
options.B: Enveloped respiratory viruses
options.C: Gram-positive cocci
options.D: Bacterial endospores

explanation: Endospores have built-in super coats that make them amazingly resistant to heat, drying, and harsh chemicals.

question: What is likely to happen if a hospital sets its DRF mark-up to zero percent?

options.A: The pharmacy will gradually lose purchasing power due to inflation and waste, leading to stock-outs
options.B: Patients will buy more drugs because they are cheaper, making the fund richer
options.C: The hospital will save money on administrative costs and paperwork
options.D: The government will send extra money every month to maintain the exact same inventory level

explanation: Without a small mark-up to cover waste and inflation, your capital gradually shrinks until you can no longer afford to restock.

question: What does morbidity measure in a community?

options.A: The state of being unhealthy or diseased
options.B: The total number of registered deaths
options.C: The number of new babies born in a year
options.D: The amount of money earned by hospitals

explanation: Morbidity focuses on illness, sickness, and disease prevalence rather than death itself. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h4)

question: How do common antipyretic drugs like paracetamol primarily lower a fever?

options.A: By blocking prostaglandin synthesis in the brain
options.B: By destroying bacteria in the bloodstream
options.C: By forcing the blood vessels in the skin to constrict
options.D: By directly cooling the skin through evaporation

explanation: Antipyretics stop the production of prostaglandins in the hypothalamus, which allows the body's internal thermostat to drop back down. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h4)

question: What document clearly lists who is responsible for specific tasks and when they are due after a meeting?

options.A: A patient care plan
options.B: A hospital discharge summary
options.C: An annual financial budget
options.D: An action log

explanation: An action log tracks follow-up tasks with clear owners and deadlines so decisions actually get done.

question: What type of prevention is a nurse practicing when teaching a patient to eat healthy to avoid illness?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Quaternary prevention

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on stopping a disease or condition from occurring in the first place through healthy lifestyle choices. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h3)

question: What practical tool can a nurse recommend to help an elderly patient who forgets daily doses?

options.A: A strict fasting diet plan
options.B: A weekly pill organizer box
options.C: A large wall calendar for appointments
options.D: A daily rigorous exercise chart

explanation: Pill boxes sorted by day and time help patients easily see whether they have taken their scheduled medications. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is the primary chemical messenger released at the neuromuscular junction to cause muscle contraction?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Dopamine
options.C: Serotonin
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the key neurotransmitter stored in nerve terminals that crosses the synaptic cleft to stimulate muscle fiber receptors. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h1)

question: What does a normal P wave tell us on an ECG?

options.A: Sudden failure of the aortic valve
options.B: Electrical activation of the atria
options.C: Complete relaxation of the whole heart
options.D: Dangerous blockage in a coronary artery

explanation: The little P wave is just the atria waking up and squeezing blood down to the ventricles. Easy peasy!
